name: Twenty
summary: Twenty is a cyber-warfare startup that raised $100 million in a June 2026 Series B at a $1 billion valuation, according to Axios.
overview: Twenty develops cyber-warfare capabilities for national-security use cases. Its Series B was led by Accel, with the financing directed toward research, development and its existing product roadmap.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Axios and the company announcement reported the Accel-led Series B and $1 billion valuation.

bull_case: Demand for cyber capabilities in national-security missions can create a high-value specialised market.
bear_case: The sector has long procurement cycles, significant policy exposure and limited public product disclosure.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: Twenty is a private company tracked by The Private Ledger in enterprise software.
company: Twenty is a cyber-warfare company building capabilities for national-security operations. In June 2026 it announced a Series B intended to accelerate research and development.
Axios reported that Accel led the $100 million financing at a $1 billion valuation, with Point72 Ventures, Caffeinated Capital and Friends & Family Capital also backing the company.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Twenty reflects investor demand for cyber capabilities tied to national security. Contract conversion and responsible operational use will be more important than its early valuation headline.

changed.text: Twenty announced a $100M Series B led by Accel at a $1B valuation.

takeaways: Twenty is a cyber-warfare company, not a conventional enterprise-software provider.
Axios reported its $100M Series B at a $1B valuation.
Procurement and contract execution are the central evidence to watch.
